title.purpose: View headings: the source title in the editor, the Library heading.

headline.purpose: Panel titles (Export) and the toolbar wordmark.

body.purpose: Default UI text, rail items, library rows, the Add to queue label.

control.purpose: Button, field and segmented option text.

caption.purpose: Field labels, queue status, details, engine state, hints.

label.purpose: Uppercase fieldset legends and group headings that name the controls beneath; never a kicker above a title.

timecode.purpose: The transport clock; mono with tabular figures.

mono.purpose: Every number, timecode, size, percentage, file name, container code and command, at the surrounding size.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: Floating messages that overlap content, such as the URL error under the toolbar field.

shadows.name: overflow-edge
shadows.purpose: The sticky More settings below bar, signalling content scrolled beneath it.

motion.purpose: All authored transforms and the queue landing.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Colour and border state changes (linear) and timeline handle widening.

motion.name: dur
motion.purpose: Transforms: mirrored preview, chevron rotation, overall progress width.

motion.name: land
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: a queued row drops 6px into place while a Cut Wash fades out.

motion.name: queued
motion.purpose: Add to queue label rises 3px from 40% opacity, echoing the landing.

motion.purpose: Applied to every element under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

components.css: .ds-tf { display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; } .ds-tf > span { font-family: var(--font-ui, 'Geist Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--text-2, #aeaeb2); } .ds-field { width: 118px; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; background: var(--bg-input, #0f0f10); border: 1px solid var(--line-strong, #3a3a3c); border-radius: 4px; color: var(--text, #f5f5f7); font-size: 12.5px; caret-color: var(--accent, #fa2d48); transition: border-color 120ms linear; } .ds-field:hover { border-color: var(--line-hover, #4a4a4e); } .ds-field:focus { border-color: var(--text-3, #8e8e93); outline: none; } .ds-field:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #fa2d48); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-field[aria-invalid='true'] { border-color: var(--danger, #ff6961); } .ds-mono { font-family: var(--font-mono, 'Geist Mono Variable', Consolas, monospace); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.css: .ds-queue { background: var(--bg-rail, #161618); width: 640px; } .ds-qrow { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 240px 64px; gap: 16px; align-items: center; height: 44px; padding: 0 12px 0 16px; border-top: 1px solid var(--line-soft, #222224); font-family: var(--font-ui, 'Geist Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 13px; color: var(--text, #f5f5f7); } .ds-qname { font-family: var(--font-mono, 'Geist Mono Variable', monospace); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-qprog { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 5px; } .ds-qbar { display: block; height: 4px; background: var(--line, #2c2c2e); } .ds-qbar > span { display: block; height: 100%; background: var(--text, #f5f5f7); transition: width 900ms linear; } .ds-qstatus { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--text-2, #aeaeb2); } .ds-qstatus span:last-child, .ds-qsize { font-family: var(--font-mono, 'Geist Mono Variable', monospace); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-qsize { font-size: 12px; color: var(--text-2, #aeaeb2); text-align: right; } .ds-fresh { animation: ds-land 900ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } @keyframes ds-land { 0% { background: rgb(250 45 72 / 0.12); transform: translateY(-6px); } 35% { transform: none; } 100% { background: transparent; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-fresh { animation-duration: 0ms; } }

components.name: Timeline
components.description: The signature: the cut range is the one region red owns.
components.css: .ds-tl { position: relative; width: 520px; height: 56px; background: var(--bg-raised, #1e1e21); border: 1px solid var(--line, #2c2c2e); border-radius: 4px; } .ds-tl-shade { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.38); } .ds-tl-range { position: absolute; top: -1px; bottom: -1px; background: var(--accent-wash, rgb(250 45 72 / 0.12)); border-top: 2px solid var(--accent, #fa2d48); border-bottom: 2px solid var(--accent, #fa2d48); } .ds-tl-handle { position: absolute; top: -1px; bottom: -1px; width: 12px; margin-left: -6px; padding: 0; border: 0; background: var(--accent, #fa2d48); border-radius: 3px; cursor: ew-resize; z-index: 1; transition: width 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), margin-left 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-tl-handle::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50%; width: 2px; height: 18px; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.8); } .ds-tl-handle:hover, .ds-tl-handle:focus-visible { width: 14px; margin-left: -7px; } .ds-tl-handle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--text, #f5f5f7); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-tl-head { position: absolute; top: -6px; bottom: -1px; width: 2px; margin-left: -1px; background: var(--text, #f5f5f7); z-index: 2; } .ds-tl-head::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 0; left: -4px; width: 10px; height: 8px; background: var(--text, #f5f5f7); clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 55%, 50% 100%, 0 55%); }

narrative.overview:
Craftora is a dark, dense desktop workbench where the cut is the hero. Everything that is not the cut is graphite: a tight ladder of near-black surfaces separated by hairline rules, with type in grey steps. Against that quiet field, red appears in exactly two jobs (the range being cut on the timeline, with its length readout, and the one primary action) so the eye always knows what is being kept and how to commit it. The dark frame is chosen by use: people judge a picture here, and a dark surround keeps the preview true.

The layout is a fixed, always-visible workspace rather than a set of tabs: toolbar across the top, a narrow rail, the editor in the centre, a fixed-width export panel on the right and the queue dock along the bottom, so running work is never hidden. Density is utility-grade: 32px controls, 12.5–13px UI text, 4px corners. Depth comes from tonal steps and 1px lines, not shadows. Motion is short and functional, with one authored moment: a queued job landing in the dock.

Confirmed rejections from the owner's brand commitments: no pill-shaped buttons, no purple, no decorative gradients, no cursor animations or scroll effects.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite surface ladder (seven steps, darkest to lightest) with hairline 1px rules.
Red is rationed: the cut range and the single primary action; the toolbar logo is an exempt brand mark.
Selection, radios, checkboxes, segmented choices and progress are neutral (white and grey), never red.
Geist for words, Geist Mono with tabular figures for every number, timecode, size and command.
Near-square corners (3–4px), no pills, no gradients.
One authored motion moment; everything else is a 120ms colour change.

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: Red does two jobs: mark the cut (range, handles, clip length) and fill the one primary action per screen. The toolbar logo is the brand mark and is exempt. Any other red is a defect.

rules.name: The Neutral Choice Rule
rules.body: A chosen state is never red. Selected rail items, checked option rows, pressed segments, radios and checkboxes (`accent-color` set to the text colour) and progress bars all use white and graphite.

rules.name: The Status Only Rule
rules.body: Green means finished, amber means warning or not connected, coral means invalid. None of them decorate.

rules.name: The Mono Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every number the user reads or types (timecodes, durations, sizes, percentages, counts, file names, container codes, the command) is set in Geist Mono with tabular figures. Words stay in Geist, even inside a mixed string.

rules.name: The No Display Face Rule
rules.body: There is no display size. The largest type is 16px; hierarchy comes from weight and grey steps.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: Panels, cards, rows and controls carry no shadow. If a surface needs separating, use a darker or lighter graphite step and a hairline.

rules.name: The Landing Rule
rules.body: The one authored motion: a newly queued row arrives with a 900ms ease-out landing, dropping 6px into place within the first 35% while a Cut Wash fades out behind it; the Add to queue label echoes it with a 600ms rise. No other element animates on entry.

dos: **Do** keep red to the cut (range, handles, clip length) and one primary button per screen; the toolbar logo is the only exempt red.
**Do** show chosen states in white and graphite: Selected Graphite fills, the strong line grey for pressed segments, text-coloured radios and checkboxes.
**Do** set every number, timecode, size, percentage and command in Geist Mono with tabular figures.
**Do** separate regions with graphite steps and 1px hairlines; use 4px corners on controls and 3px on their inner parts.
**Do** size controls at 32px and space on the 4px scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 20).
**Do** keep running work visible: the queue dock never collapses out of the layout.
**Do** make motion short and functional (120ms colour, 220ms ease-out transforms) and zero it under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** use red for chosen states (selected items, radios, pressed segments), progress, links, badges or decoration.
**Don't** use pill-shaped buttons or radii beyond 4px on rectangles.
**Don't** add cursor animations or scroll effects.
**Don't** put shadows on panels, rows or controls; shadows are for popovers and the overflow edge only.
**Don't** use green, amber or coral for anything but finished, warning/not-connected and invalid.
**Don't** add a display type size; the largest text is 16px.
